location.mountain: Western Caucasus Foothills, Matsesta River Valley

description.short: A local variety of Krasnodar tea from the Matsesta valley with a gentle herbal character
description.overview: Matsesta is a Sochi district historically famed for hydrogen sulfide mineral springs and sanatorium medicine, which also developed as an early center of Russian tea growing.
description.taste: Light-bodied, soft, with delicate herbal nuances

history.origin: The Matsesta River valley became one of the key areas where tea farming was established in the early 20th century alongside flourishing balneological resort infrastructure.
history.development: The region's tea heritage stems from Iuda Koshman's pioneering experiments acclimating tea bushes to the Black Sea Caucasus coast.
history.modern: Today Matsesta tea is a recognized local sub-brand within Sochi/Krasnodar tea, often sold as part of the regional health resort and artisanal tourist offerings.
interestingFacts: Matsesta is renowned worldwide for therapeutic sulfur baths and historical Soviet sanatoriums, somewhat overshadowing its status as a cradle of Russian tea growing.
The parallel development of tea farming and spa medicine makes Matsesta an unusual cultural junction of agro-heritage and wellness history.
